_readme: THE INK PALETTES for the poster design.
Every section of the site is a screen print in three inks on one paper stock.
Scrolling from one section to the next cross-fades the whole page between palettes,
which is the colour-theory idea made into the interface.
paper   the stock everything prints on (page background)
ink     the darkest colour — all body text and the heavy shapes
accent  the loud one — headlines, the brand voice, big shapes
pop     the third ink — small marks, highlights, punctuation
Photographs stay in full colour and get mounted like prints — a paper mat in the
section's inks, a caption block, a Pantone chip. The frame does the art direction
so the food can carry on looking edible.
TO RETUNE A SECTION: change its hexes here and re-run  python build_poster.py.
Nothing else needs touching — the artwork is SVG and takes its colour from CSS.
Pantone codes are the nearest published match, printed on the site as chips.
TWO RULES, both learned the hard way:
1. FOOD IS ALWAYS WARM. 'accent' and 'pop' are the warm inks and the food wears them.
'ink' is the cool ground it sits on. A cool-inked pizza stops looking edible, and a
duotoned photograph of meat looks spoiled — we tried it, it was unusable.
2. 'ink' carries every piece of text. 'accent' is display sizes only (it clears 3:1,
not 4.5:1, on paper). 'pop' never carries text at all.

house.note: The shop's own red, anchored by cobalt so it reads confident instead of loud.

donair.name: Spit & Sauce
donair.note: Aubergine and terracotta — the colour of the meat cone and the sauce.

harbour.name: Harbour
harbour.note: Deep Atlantic teal against a coral that only a seafood counter earns.

latenight.name: Two AM
latenight.note: Midnight ground, hot red food, and a magenta that only marks and badges get to wear.

_sectionReadme: Which palette each part of the page prints in, top to bottom.
_photoReadme: Which palette each photo is MOUNTED in — the mat and caption around it, not the photo itself. '_default' catches anything not listed.
